answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashed stake. Each new agent identity must lock real collateral before it can vote or earn. A double-vote or forged attestation destroys the bond, like burning the timber holding up a structure. Because every fake identity needs its own deposit, an attacker wanting a thousand votes must lock a thousand separate stakes, so the cost grows linearly with the attack. A farm calling itself nebula or hiding each node behind a falcon alias still cannot mint influence cheaply: once fraud is caught its capital is burned, making a large Sybil attack uneconomical.
